title: TB-AI: Automated Detection of Acid-Fast Bacilli from Ziehl Neelsen-Stained Sputum Smear Microscopy Using EfficientNet-Based Computer Vision and HiResCAM Heatmapping
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the leading infectious causes of death worldwide, with the greatest burden occurring in low- and middle-income countries. Although molecular diagnostic tests have expanded access to rapid diagnosis, Ziehl Neelsen-stained sputum smear microscopy remains the most widely used frontline diagnostic method in resource-limited settings because of its affordability and accessibility. However, manual microscopy is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and susceptible to inter-observer variability, contributing to delayed diagnosis and treatment. This study presents TB-AI, an artificial intelligence-based diagnostic platform designed to support automated tuberculosis detection from sputum smear microscopy.
METHODS: TB-AI utilizes an EfficientNet-based convolutional neural network for automated detection of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) from Ziehl Neelsen-stained sputum smear microscopy images. The model was developed using 45,000 annotated microscopy images, including 30,000 pre-annotated images acquired using conventional brightfield microscopy and 15,000 high-resolution digital microscopy images obtained from collaborating clinical laboratories and publicly available datasets. Ground-truth annotations were provided by experienced microbiologists. Images were divided into training (70%), validation (15%), and testing (15%) datasets. Image augmentation techniques, including rotation, scaling, normalization, and contrast adjustment, were applied to enhance model generalization. HiResCAM heatmapping was incorporated to generate high-resolution activation maps highlighting image regions contributing to model predictions.
RESULTS: TB-AI achieved a sensitivity of 98.5%, specificity of 97.2%, and an overall accuracy of 97.9% for automated AFB detection. HiResCAM heatmaps consistently localized image regions associated with AFB, supporting interpretation of model predictions, while EfficientNet demonstrated robust performance across heterogeneous microscopy image sources. These findings suggest that the framework can provide accurate and reliable assistance for smear microscopy interpretation.
CONCLUSION: TB-AI demonstrates the potential of combining EfficientNet-based computer vision with HiResCAM heatmapping to enhance tuberculosis diagnosis from Ziehl Neelsen-stained sputum smear microscopy images. By supporting standardized interpretation, reducing reliance on manual microscopy, and improving laboratory efficiency, the platform offers a scalable approach for strengthening TB diagnostic services in resource-constrained healthcare settings. Future studies will focus on prospective multicentre clinical validation and integration into routine tuberculosis laboratory workflows.

title: A Stroke Prediction Model In Imbalanced Data: The Case of an Improved Cost Function for Logistic Regression
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a major non-communicable disease and a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally. Early identification of individuals at increased risk of stroke can support timely prevention and intervention. However, developing accurate prediction models is challenging when stroke cases are substantially underrepresented relative to non-stroke cases. Conventional classification methods may therefore be biased toward the majority class, resulting in poor identification of individuals at risk of stroke. This study aimed to compare the performance of the Binary Logistic Regression, balanced logistic regression, and the Grid Search Regularized Weighted Logistic Regression (GSRWLR) models, which integrate class weighting, L2 regularization, and grid search for hyperparameter tuning, using 5,110 records from Kaggle's Stroke Prediction Dataset (2020).
RESULT: Findings revealed that the Binary Logistic regression model had poor sensitivity (1.33%), identifying only one stroke case; the balanced logistic regression improved to 77.33%. GSRWLR further enhanced recall to 93.33%, though Area Under Curve-Receiver Operating Characteristic (AUC-ROC) values were similar across models (approximately 0.83), indicating comparable overall classification ability. GSRWLR demonstrated superior performance in identifying rare events. Age, heart disease, average glucose level, and hypertension were identified as key predictors of stroke.
CONCLUSION: from the study suggest that optimizing logistic regression with regularization, class weighting, and grid search significantly improves stroke prediction in imbalanced datasets. Health systems could utilize Grid Search Regularized Weighted Logistic Regression to enhance the detection of stroke, particularly in under-resourced environments such as Ugandan hospitals. Further research using routinely collected clinical data from Uganda and other African populations is needed to externally validate the model and assess its potential application in local health systems.

title: Using AI to Close the Communication Gap in Hospital Discharge: A Frontline-Built NHS Solution
abstract:
Introduction: Hospital discharge delays are a recurring issue in many healthcare systems, including the NHS. Patients who are medically fit to leave hospital are often delayed simply because the organisations involved in discharge planning don't share systems or communicate well with each other. Fragmented communication between these organisations has been identified as one of the leading causes of discharge delay. This puts more strain on hospital beds, disrupts patient flow, and causes unnecessary stress for patients, families and staff. Hospitals often have excellent internal electronic records, but that visibility disappears once discharge involves outside organisations.
Objective: To present the design of EO HealthHub Connect, an AI-enabled platform built from frontline NHS experience to close these communication gaps and support safer, faster hospital discharge.
Methods: The platform was shaped directly by frontline NHS discharge work. We ran a structured survey of 66 healthcare professionals involved in discharge across the pathway, asking what caused delays, where communication broke down, and where technology could help. These findings, combined with day-to-day clinical experience, shaped the design of the Minimum Viable Product, which is currently in development. Innovation: EO HealthHub Connect is a cloud-based SaaS platform, enabled by AI, that gives hospitals, local authorities, community providers, and other services a shared digital space to plan and coordinate discharge together. Patients and families are also included on the platform, so they can stay informed and involved in their own discharge process rather than relying only on phone calls for updates. The platform is built to close the communication gap between everyone involved and give a clearer, more connected view of a patient's discharge journey. AI supports the platform by streamlining workflows, but clinical decisions stay firmly with healthcare professionals.
Expected Impact: The platform hasn't been piloted yet, but it's been designed to directly address problems identified by frontline staff and stakeholders. Once implemented, it should improve communication between organisations, strengthen coordination across health and social care, and make discharge faster and less stressful for patients, families, and staff. This approach could also be useful for other healthcare providers facing the same problem.
Conclusion: Frontline healthcare staff see the everyday breakdowns in patient care up close, which puts them in a strong position to build practical solutions. EO HealthHub Connect is an example of clinical experience, stakeholder input and digital design coming together to solve a real problem in the NHS. Next steps are piloting the platform, evaluating it with real discharge teams, and refining it based on what we learn.

title: Early Diagnosis of Ischemic Stroke on Non-Contrast CT Scans Using Artificial Intelligence: Development and Evaluation of a CNN-Based Decision Support System in Uganda
abstract:
Background: Timely diagnosis of ischemic stroke remains a major challenge in many low-resource settings due to shortages of specialist radiologists and increasing imaging workloads. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers opportunities to support rapid image interpretation and strengthen health service delivery. This study developed and evaluated a convolutional neural network (CNN) for automated detection of early ischemic stroke on non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) scans and implemented the model within a web-based decision support platform.
Methods: A retrospective dataset of NCCT scans obtained from Mulago National Referral Hospital was used to train and evaluate the CNN model. Images underwent preprocessing, including intensity normalization and feature enhancement, before model development. Performance was assessed using five-fold cross-validation and compared with a senior radiologist on an independent evaluation subset. A web-based platform was developed to facilitate image upload and automated analysis.
Results: The CNN achieved a mean accuracy of 90.2%, sensitivity of 91.4%, specificity of 89.0%, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 91.3% across five-fold cross-validation. On an independent comparison dataset, the model demonstrated competitive performance relative to a senior radiologist while producing results in approximately three seconds per scan compared with approximately five minutes for manual interpretation. The web-based platform successfully generated automated predictions and confidence scores, demonstrating the feasibility of integrating AI-assisted stroke detection into routine clinical workflows.
Conclusion: The study demonstrates the potential of locally developed AI solutions to support early ischemic stroke diagnosis using routinely available NCCT imaging. By reducing interpretation time and providing rapid decision support, the system may contribute to strengthening health service delivery and improving access to timely stroke care in resource-constrained settings. Further multicenter validation is recommended prior to large-scale deployment.

title: Design and Development of a Hierarchical Confidence Weighted Ensemble Learning Framework for Speech Disorder in Children
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Speech and language disorders in pediatric populations can adversely affect communication, learning, cognitive development, and social interaction, making early and accurate diagnosis essential for effective intervention. This study proposes a Hierarchical Confidence-Weighted Ensemble (HCWE) framework for the classification of pediatric therapeutic speech disorders using linguistic and statistical speech-derived features extracted from the CHILDES dataset.
METHODS: The proposed framework integrates multiple calibrated machine learning classifiers, including Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Logistic Regression, within a hierarchical stacking architecture that combines classifier outputs using confidence-weighted probability fusion. To improve predictive performance and generalization, the framework incorporates comprehensive data preprocessing, class balancing using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), and hybrid feature optimization based on Mutual Information (MI) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). The proposed HCWE was evaluated using standard performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), calibration analysis, and computational efficiency, while Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques were employed to identify the most influential linguistic features contributing to classification decisions.
RESULTS: Experimental results demonstrate that the HCWE framework consistently outperforms individual machine learning models by achieving higher classification accuracy, superior probability calibration, improved robustness, and enhanced predictive reliability in distinguishing Typically Developing (TD) children from those with Specific Language Impairment (SLI).
CONCLUSION: By integrating hierarchical confidence-weighted ensemble learning, linguistic and statistical feature fusion, probability calibration, and explainable AI within a unified framework, the proposed approach provides an accurate, interpretable, and clinically reliable decision-support system for the early identification of pediatric speech and language disorders.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Youth Sexual and Reproductive Health Literacy: Evidence from an AI Chatbot Intervention in Abuja, Nigeria

authors.name: Media, Health & Rights Initiative of Nigeria (MHR)

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited access to accurate and confidential information on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) is still a major issue facing young people in Nigeria. Stigma, cultural issues, and limited availability of youth-friendly health services contribute to this. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities to address these issues. The objective of this study was to evaluate how effective an AI-based health chatbot is in improving knowledge of SRHR among selected men and women in Gwagwalada Area Council Abuja.
METHODS: A mixed-methods research design was adopted. The study population comprised 100 selected men and women from the age of 18 to 40 years who resides in Gwagwalada Area Council, Abuja. Quantitative data were collected using a structured Likert-scale questionnaire, while qualitative data were obtained through focus group discussions (FGDs) involving 50 participants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, mean scores, and chi-square tests to examine associations between AI usage and SRHR literacy outcomes. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically.
RESULTS: The results show that 92% of the participants owned or used a smartphone regularly, and 78% of the participants had previous experience with AI chatbots. The participants believed that the AI health chatbot had a significant positive impact on them. On average, the participants' knowledge of sexual and reproductive health was rated 4.21 (SD = 0.63), while the participants' ability to obtain accurate health information was rated 4.18 (SD = 0.67). The results of the chi-square analysis showed that there was a significant association between the use of AI and the improvement of participants' knowledge of SRH (chi-square = 18.47, p less than 0.05). Moreover, the results showed that there was a significant association between the use of AI and the improvement of participants' confidence in making health decisions (chi-square = 16.32, p less than 0.05). The participants' satisfaction with the AI chatbot was high; the average rating was 4.26 (SD = 0.59). Moreover, the participants' willingness to recommend the AI chatbot was high; the average rating was 4.19 (SD = 0.61). The focus group discussions showed that the participants were satisfied with the AI chatbot because of its privacy, anonymity, and ease of use.
DISCUSSION/CONCLUSION: The findings demonstrate that AI-based health chatbots can significantly improve SRHR knowledge and decision-making confidence among adults in Gwagwalada Area Council, Abuja. High smartphone ownership and familiarity with AI facilitated accessibility and use. Participants valued the chatbot's privacy, anonymity, and ease of use, which reduced stigma-related barriers to seeking information. Overall, AI-driven chatbots are effective tools for promoting SRHR literacy, enhancing confidential access to health information, and strengthening community-level health system responsiveness. Integrating scalable AI platforms into public health strategies could advance equity, reduce informational gaps, and complement existing service delivery models in Nigeria and similar contexts.

title: From Preferences to Precision: Human Centered Evidence for AI-Enabled HIV Care Engagement among Men Living with HIV in Nigeria
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being integrated into HIV service delivery through personalized patient engagement and automated communication. However, AI enabled communication systems require empirical evidence on patient communication preferences to support context aware personalization, particularly in low-resource settings. This study explored HIV information exposure and communication preferences among heterosexual men and men who have sex with men (MSM) over the preceding 12 months to generate the human centered evidence needed for developing AI enabled patient engagement systems.
METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study among 640 men living with HIV in Ibadan, Nigeria. 160 HIV-positive MSM were recruited using respondent driven sampling (RDS), while 480 HIV-positive heterosexual men were recruited from ART clinics using convenience sampling. Data was collected using a semi-structured interviewer administered questionnaire assessing exposure to HIV information sources. Focus group discussions (FGDs) were conducted using an FGD guide to explore preferences for receiving reminders via SMS or phone calls for antiretroviral drug pickup and clinic follow up. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics at alpha 0.05, while qualitative data were analysed thematically.
RESULTS: The mean age of heterosexual men was 43.1 plus/minus 8.67 years, while MSM were 26.4 plus/minus 5.82 years (p less than 0.001). Health workers were the predominant HIV information source among heterosexual men (78.8% vs 30.0%, p less than 0.001), followed by television (39.0%) and radio (38.8%). Internet use was the main source among MSM, compared to heterosexuals (70.6% vs 5.0%, p less than 0.05), while peer educators (50.0%), radio (34.4%) and NGOs (21.9%) also featured prominently. Qualitative findings revealed divergent communication preferences: heterosexual men preferred phone calls for confidentiality and direct interaction, whereas MSM preferred SMS for confidentiality, discretion and convenience.
CONCLUSION: These findings provide foundational human centered evidence for developing AI enabled communication systems capable of dynamically selecting reminder channels according to clients' demographic characteristics, information channel exposure and confidentiality concerns. The identified communication patterns, spanning interactive voice response (IVR) and SMS modalities, could serve as inputs for future machine learning or reinforcement learning models that personalize reminder delivery, with the potential to improve medication adherence, clinic attendance and long term retention in HIV care in resource limited settings.

title: Streamlining Healthcare Workflows: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence Automation to Eliminate Operational Time Bottlenecks
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Modern healthcare systems face severe operational challenges, primarily driven by a crisis of time management. Clinicians and administrative staff routinely spend a disproportionate amount of their working hours on documentation, data entry, and scheduling rather than direct patient care. This administrative burden accelerates clinician burnout, increases clinical errors, and significantly delays patient treatment timelines.
METHODS: This study evaluates the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) automation frameworks designed to optimize time allocation within clinical workflows. We implemented and analyzed automated AI systems across three primary domains: ambient clinical intelligence for automated medical scribing, predictive algorithms for optimized patient scheduling, and natural language processing (NLP) tools for expedited prior-authorization processing. Data was collected across a six-month pilot period to measure reductions in task-completion times, patient wait times, and administrative overhead compared to traditional manual baselines.
RESULT: The deployment of AI automation yielded statistically significant time savings across all tested areas. Ambient AI scribing reduced clinical documentation time by 45%, saving physicians an average of 2.1 hours per day. Furthermore, predictive scheduling algorithms decreased patient wait times by 30% and minimized clinic scheduling gaps. Most notably, the AI-driven prior-authorization system cut insurance approval processing times from an average of 4.5 days down to less than 24 hours, dramatically accelerating the delivery of critical patient interventions.
CONCLUSION: Artificial intelligence automation serves as a powerful tool to solve critical time deficits in healthcare delivery. By systematically replacing manual, repetitive administrative burdens with intelligent automation, healthcare facilities can reclaim valuable hours for medical staff. This structural shift not only enhances operational efficiency and reduces institutional costs, but it also improves patient outcomes by allowing providers to refocus their time on direct, empathetic patient care.

title: Addressing Radiologist Shortages in Low-Resource Settings using WGAN-GP Synthetic Data Augmentation and Lightweight Deep Learning for COVID-19 and Respiratory Disease Diagnosis from Chest X-rays
abstract: Chest X-ray remains the most accessible tool for diagnosing COVID-19 and respiratory disease, yet in low-resource settings across Africa, the near-absence of radiologists means most patients never receive a timely or accurate read. AI-assisted interpretation offers a viable solution, but reliable diagnostic models require large labelled datasets that most African health facilities cannot produce. This study investigated whether Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) synthetic augmentation combined with lightweight attention-enhanced deep learning can deliver accurate multi-class respiratory disease classification without dependence on large labelled datasets. The COVID-19 Radiography Dataset was used, comprising four classes: COVID-19, Lung Opacity, Normal, and Viral Pneumonia, balanced to 5,000 images per class and split 80:20 for training and validation. A WGAN-GP was trained for 500 epochs, generating 5,000 synthetic images per class to augment 4,000 real training images. Two lightweight architectures were evaluated MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2 each enhanced with Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) and Local Region Self-Attention (LRSA) modules, trained under real-only and real plus synthetic conditions, and evaluated on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification across linear, RBF, and polynomial kernels was also performed. MobileNetV2 + ECA+LRSA achieved 96.73% accuracy (F1: 0.9673) with WGAN-GP augmentation, while ShuffleNetV2 + ECA+LRSA reached 95.85% (F1: 0.9585), both substantially outperforming ResNet-18 (86.19%), VGG-16 (75.36%), and traditional SVM (68.15%) benchmarks. ShuffleNetV2 converged in just 35 epochs at 5.4MB model size. RBF-kernel SVM on PCA-reduced MobileNetV2 features reached 96.55% accuracy. These results demonstrate that lightweight attention-enhanced models trained on modest datasets, supported by WGAN-GP augmentation, can achieve deployable diagnostic accuracy for respiratory disease within the data and infrastructure constraints common across African health systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Post-Stroke Epilepsy: A Scoping Review of Imaging Based Prediction Models and Implications for African Settings
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke seizures (PSS) and post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) are important neurological complications associated with poorer functional recovery, increased mortality, and reduced quality of life after stroke. Neuroimaging plays a central role in identifying patients at increased risk, and recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled the development of imaging-based prediction models that may improve individualized risk stratification. However, the current evidence remains fragmented, and the extent to which these approaches are applicable to African healthcare settings is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This scoping review mapped the global evidence on imaging-based AI models developed to predict PSS and PSE, characterized the neuroimaging modalities, computational methods, and validation strategies employed, and examined the representation of African populations to identify opportunities and challenges for future implementation.
Methods: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following the PRISMA-ScR guideline. Searches of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar identified studies that used CT, MRI, radiomics, or multimodal neuroimaging with imaging-based AI approaches, including machine learning, radiomics, and deep learning, to predict seizure-related outcomes after stroke. Data were charted on study characteristics, imaging modalities, computational methods, validation strategies, prediction outcomes, and geographical representation.
RESULTS: Twenty-three studies published between 2005 and 2026 met the eligibility criteria. The evidence demonstrated a clear methodological evolution from conventional imaging-based prediction models to radiomics, machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI, and multimodal approaches. MRI and CT were the predominant imaging modalities, with cortical involvement, lesion location, infarct volume, haemorrhagic transformation, and quantitative radiomic features emerging as the most frequently reported imaging predictors. Most AI models relied on internal validation, while relatively few underwent external validation. The evidence base was concentrated in East Asia, Europe, and North America, with no eligible imaging-based AI model developed or externally validated using African datasets.
CONCLUSION: Imaging-based AI for predicting PSS and PSE has progressed rapidly, but important methodological and geographical gaps remain. Limited external validation, heterogeneous reporting, and the absence of African development and validation cohorts restrict confidence in the generalisability of existing models. Future research should prioritise multicentre, externally validated, and explainable imaging-based AI models developed using representative African neuroimaging datasets to support equitable clinical translation.

title: Hormona: An AI-Powered Platform for Early Hormonal Health Risk Assessment and Women's Health Service Delivery
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hormonal health disorders, including Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), endometriosis, thyroid disorders, and menstrual irregularities, affect millions of women worldwide. Many women experience delayed diagnosis due to limited awareness, stigma, fragmented health information, and unequal access to healthcare services. Existing digital health solutions often focus primarily on menstrual tracking and provide limited support for comprehensive hormonal health awareness and early risk identification. There is a need for accessible, AI-enabled tools that empower women with personalized health information while supporting healthcare systems through preventive care.
METHODS: Hormona was developed as an AI-powered digital health platform designed to strengthen health service delivery by promoting early hormonal health awareness. The platform integrates menstrual and symptom tracking, AI-powered risk assessment, personalized lifestyle and nutrition recommendations, and evidence based educational resources. Privacy preserving data practices are incorporated to protect user information while enabling anonymized health data to contribute to future research and public health insights.
RESULTS: As a prototype, Hormona demonstrates the feasibility of integrating artificial intelligence into women's hormonal healthcare. The platform provides users with personalized insights based on reported symptoms, encourages timely consultation with healthcare professionals, and supports informed decision making. By moving beyond traditional period tracking applications, Hormona offers a more comprehensive approach to hormonal health education and preventive care while generating anonymized datasets that can improve the representation of women, particularly those from underserved communities, in health research.
CONCLUSION: Hormona demonstrates the potential of AI to strengthen health systems through accessible, user-centered digital health services. By promoting early risk awareness, improving health literacy, and supporting data driven research, the platform contributes to more equitable and preventive women's healthcare. Future work will focus on clinical validation, partnerships with healthcare providers, multilingual support, and integration with national digital health ecosystems to enhance scalability and long term impact.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Transform Comprehensive Postpartum Care and Strengthen Maternal Health Systems in Nigeria
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The postpartum period is one of the most critical yet underserved phases of the maternal health continuum. In Nigeria, many women experience preventable complications such as postpartum hypertension, infection, depression, poor breastfeeding outcomes, and delayed recognition of danger signs after discharge from health facilities. Limited access to continuous postpartum support, particularly in underserved communities, contributes to avoidable maternal morbidity and mortality. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) present an opportunity to bridge these gaps by providing personalised, accessible, and scalable postpartum care that complements existing health services and supports progress towards Universal Health Coverage (UHC).
METHODS: This paper presents a conceptual framework for an AI-enabled digital postpartum care platform designed to strengthen continuity of maternal care beyond childbirth. The proposed platform integrates AI-powered symptom assessment, personalised breastfeeding support, mental health screening, blood pressure and blood glucose monitoring, medication and appointment reminders, health education, and timely referral recommendations. The framework draws on current evidence in digital health, maternal health guidelines, and user-centred design principles to address the unique needs of postpartum women in Nigeria while supporting integration with primary healthcare services.
RESULT: The proposed model demonstrates how AI can improve early identification of postpartum complications, promote healthy breastfeeding practices, enhance maternal self-management, and facilitate timely referral to healthcare providers. By delivering personalised health information and continuous remote support, the platform has the potential to improve adherence to postpartum care recommendations, reduce delays in seeking care, and strengthen communication between mothers and healthcare professionals. The approach also offers opportunities for anonymised data collection to support health system planning, resource allocation, and maternal health surveillance.
CONCLUSION: Artificial intelligence has the potential to transform postpartum care from episodic, facility-based encounters into continuous, patient-centred support that extends into the community. Integrating AI-driven solutions within Nigeria's maternal healthcare system can enhance service delivery, improve maternal and newborn outcomes, and contribute to stronger, more resilient health systems. As Nigeria accelerates its digital health agenda, AI-enabled postpartum care represents a promising innovation for advancing maternal health and achieving Universal Health Coverage across the country and the wider African region.

title: Explainable AI for Multi-Class Chest X-ray Classification: A Decision-Support Framework for Low-Resource Healthcare in Nigeria
abstract: Chest X-ray interpretation remains essential for diagnosing respiratory diseases such as tuberculosis, pneumonia, and COVID-19 in Nigeria, yet many healthcare facilities face limited access to radiologists. Although artificial intelligence has shown promise in automated image interpretation, most existing systems function as "black boxes," limiting clinician trust and adoption, particularly in low-resource settings. This work presents an explainable artificial intelligence framework for multi-class chest X-ray decision support using Nigerian clinical imaging data. The proposed system employs a fine-tuned DenseNet121 model to classify chest radiographs into Normal, Pneumonia, Tuberculosis, and COVID-19, while integrating Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) and bounding-box localization to visually explain each prediction. Beyond classification, the framework is deployed as an accessible web-based application that combines diagnostic predictions with interpretable visual evidence, supporting clinicians rather than replacing their judgment. By emphasizing transparency, local relevance, and accessibility, this study demonstrates how explainable AI can contribute to trustworthy and context-appropriate diagnostic support for strengthening clinical confidence in Nigeria.

title: TB-AI: AI-Enabled Tuberculosis Diagnosis for Decentralized Health Systems
abstract:
Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the leading infectious causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with delayed diagnosis continuing to impede disease control, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Dependence on manual microscopy, limited laboratory infrastructure, and shortages of skilled personnel contribute to delayed case detection and treatment initiation. Artificial intelligence has the potential to strengthen decentralized health systems by improving the accuracy, efficiency, and accessibility of tuberculosis diagnosis while supporting timely clinical decision-making.
Methods: TB-AI is an AI-enabled diagnostic platform that utilizes computer vision to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis from Brightfield microscopy images. The platform was developed and evaluated using 45,000 expert-annotated digital microscopy images, comprising 30,000 pre-diagnosed clinical and publicly available images supplemented by an additional 15,000 digital microscope images to improve model robustness during training. EfficientNet-based deep learning models were employed for image classification, while HiResCAM heatmapping was integrated to provide visual explanations of model predictions, enhancing interpretability and clinician confidence.
Results: TB-AI achieved a sensitivity of 95% and specificity of 98.75% for tuberculosis detection, with an overall diagnostic accuracy 97.8%. The platform demonstrates the potential to standardize microscopy interpretation, reduce dependence on highly specialized laboratory personnel, and accelerate diagnostic workflows across decentralized healthcare settings. Its explainable AI capabilities further support transparency and facilitate clinician adoption.
Conclusion: TB-AI demonstrates the potential of AI-enabled diagnostics to strengthen decentralized health systems through earlier, more reliable tuberculosis detection. By combining high diagnostic performance with explainable computer vision, the platform offers a scalable approach for improving laboratory efficiency and expanding access to quality diagnostics in high-burden settings. These findings support the integration of AI into routine tuberculosis services as part of country-led digital health strategies aimed at strengthening resilient and equitable health systems.

title: Diabetes Risk Detection Using Machine Learning: A Clinical Aid for Accurate Diagnosis and Preventive Care
abstract: Diabetes mellitus continues to grow as a worldwide public health problems, leading to a wide range of serious problems such as heart disease, nerve damage, kidney failure and loss of vision. Early detection of this disease even before the development of complication remains a big hurdles in the health-care system. The study consist of two supervised machine learning models, Logistic Regression and Random Forest, to predict the risk of the diabetes using the Healthcare Diabetes Dataset obtained from Kaggle, which contains 2,768 patient records and nine clinical features. The data was preprocessed through missing value imputation, min-max normalization, and an 80:20 ratio split to train-test to ensure the results can be reproduced. Each of the model were trained and the performance metrics is evaluated. Metrics include accuracy, precision, recall and F1 Score. Random Forest model attained the accuracy of 92%, precision of 87%, recall of 86% and F1 Score of 87%. On the other hand, Logistic Regression attained the accuracy of 80%, precision of 67%, recall of 59%, and F1 Score of 63%. The best indicator include Glucose level, BMI and age. The result suggest that Random forest is better suited than Logistic Regression for this task and could support clinical efforts to identify high risk patient earlier. Study limitation, including the demographic makeup of the dataset and the absence of real world clinical are discussed.

title: Leveraging Inclusive Digital Health Innovation to Address the Triple Threat of GBV, HIV Infection, and Adolescent Pregnancies in Nigeria
abstract:
Background: Adolescent girls and young women in Nigeria face a persistent triple burden of sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), Reproductive Infections like HIV infection, and unintended pregnancies. According to the National Agency for the Control of AIDS, young women account for a disproportionate share of new HIV infections. The National Demographic and Health Survey reports that approximately 19% of girls aged 15-19 have begun childbearing, while one in three women experience gender-based violence. These outcomes are driven by limited access to accurate health information, stigma, cultural values, financial barriers, and delayed care-seeking, particularly in underserved communities. Objectives This intervention aims to develop and pilot HerGuard, an inclusive digital health platform designed to: 1. Improve access to accurate, timely reproductive health information and medical guidance. 2. Provide a first-level digital "first aid" support system for early identification of reproductive and sexually transmitted infections. 3. Increase health-seeking behaviour through referrals and financial support. 4. Create safe, confidential spaces for support related to SGBV and mental health.
Methodology: HerGuard is currently at the idea stage and will be developed and piloted upon securing funding. The platform will adopt a three-fold approach: (1) a symptom-based digital check-up system, where users respond to guided questions that function as a first-aid health support tool, helping them understand possible symptoms, receive immediate guidance, and prepare for informed interactions with healthcare providers; (2) safe and confidential digital spaces offering peer support, mental health resources, and guidance on SGBV; and (3) facilitated access to care, including referrals and targeted financial support for treatment The platform will be designed with inclusion at its core, incorporating multilingual content, low-data functionality, and accessibility features for users with varying literacy levels and disabilities. Community-driven engagement strategies will support adoption in underserved populations.
Results (Expected Outcomes): Within 12 months of pilot implementation, HerGuard is expected to: Reach at least 5,000 women and girls aged 15-35 Achieve 60% engagement with platform features Facilitate 1,000 health-seeking actions Provide financial support to at least 1000 users Improve early identification and response to reproductive health concerns
Replication: HerGuard is designed as a scalable, low-cost, and adaptable model that can be replicated across Nigeria and Sub-Saharan Africa. Its mobile-first, inclusive design and first-aid digital support approach make it particularly suitable for resource-constrained settings. With localization and strategic partnerships, the platform can be expanded to address broader reproductive health challenges across diverse populations. By serving as a digital first aid system for women's health, HerGuard has the potential to turn uncertainty into clarity, silence into action, and vulnerability into empowered, life-saving decisions.

title: CliMED Safe: One Intelligent E-Prescription Platform for Safer, Smarter and Climate-Ready OPDs
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Outpatient prescribing in India often occurs under intense workload, fragmented documentation, variable adherence to updated guidelines and limited access to real-time clinical decision support. These gaps contribute to medication errors, inappropriate antimicrobial use, delayed recognition of deterioration and missed opportunities to protect patients during heatwaves and hazardous air-pollution events.
OBJECTIVE: To develop ClimEd Safe, an AI-enabled e-prescription and clinical decision-support platform designed for integration across hospital outpatient departments, including resource-constrained healthcare settings. Platform Design: ClimEd Safe converts routine OPD documentation into a structured, legible and interoperable electronic prescription. Based on the patient's age, diagnosis, comorbidities, allergies, pregnancy status, renal or hepatic risk and current medications, the platform provides explainable clinical prompts for appropriate drug selection, dosage, contraindications, interactions, duplicate therapy and necessary monitoring. A continuously updated guideline module enables clinicians to access relevant national and international recommendations within the prescribing workflow. An integrated antimicrobial-stewardship engine supports syndrome-based antibiotic selection, allergy checks, dose optimisation, duration guidance, culture-review prompts, de-escalation and locally configurable antibiogram-based recommendations. The platform also incorporates early-warning systems using symptoms, vital signs and available investigations to identify patients requiring urgent assessment, referral or escalation. Its climate-health module links temperature, humidity and air-quality alerts with individual vulnerability to provide preventive advice, medication-related cautions and facility-level preparedness notifications. Clinicians retain final decision-making authority, with transparent recommendations, audit trails, role-based access, data minimisation and periodic bias and performance evaluation.
CONCLUSION: ClimEd Safe makes AI real by improving every prescription, responsible by supporting rather than replacing clinicians, and revolutionary by transforming the hospital OPD into a connected centre for safer prescribing, antimicrobial stewardship, early detection and climate-resilient healthcare. ClimEd Safe does not merely digitise a prescription-it places the latest evidence, an early-warning system and a patient-safety shield inside every clinical encounter.

title: MAMMOAI: AN AI-DRIVEN FRAMEWORK FOR EARLY BREAST CANCER DETECTION AMONG AFRICAN WOMEN USING MAMMOGRAM ANALYSIS
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer among women worldwide and remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. In Africa, it accounts for approximately 16% of all female cancers, with more than 70% of cases diagnosed at advanced stages, substantially reducing treatment options and survival rates. Delayed diagnosis is driven by limited access to screening services, shortages of trained radiologists, inadequate diagnostic infrastructure, and socio-economic barriers. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, have demonstrated considerable potential for improving the accuracy and efficiency of medical image analysis. However, most existing AI models have been developed using non-African datasets and often lack the interpretability required for clinical adoption. This study proposes MAMMOAI, an AI-driven framework designed to support early breast cancer detection among African women through accurate, interpretable, and clinically deployable deep learning models.
METHODS: A quantitative experimental design will be employed using BI-RADS-labelled mammographic datasets. Images will undergo preprocessing, including resizing, normalization, contrast enhancement, and data augmentation to improve model robustness while maintaining class balance. The proposed framework integrates a hybrid ResNet50-Transformer backbone to capture complementary spatial and contextual features from mammograms. A multi-task learning architecture with five task-specific branches will simultaneously perform breast cancer risk assessment, lesion detection, disease staging, risk factor analysis, and differential diagnosis using weighted categorical cross-entropy loss functions. Model performance will be evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC). Clinical interpretability will be enhanced through Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) and uncertainty quantification, while automated HTML-based reports will provide clinician-friendly decision support.
EXPECTED RESULTS: The proposed framework is expected to achieve high diagnostic accuracy across multiple breast cancer prediction tasks while providing transparent visual explanations to support clinical decision-making. The integration of multi-task learning and explainable AI is anticipated to improve diagnostic consistency, reduce false-positive and false-negative classifications, and facilitate adoption in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
CONCLUSION: MAMMOAI presents a scalable and interpretable AI framework for early breast cancer detection tailored to African healthcare contexts. By combining advanced deep learning, explainable AI, and automated clinical reporting, the framework has the potential to strengthen diagnostic capacity, support radiologists, promote earlier detection, and ultimately contribute to reducing breast cancer mortality among African women.

title: Testing LLM Diagnostics in Endodontics: The Impact of Linguistic Variation on Unseen Cases
abstract:
Aim: To assess the diagnostic performance of two language models, GPT-5 Plus and Gemini 2.5 Flash using a curated benchmark dataset of unseen endodontic and restorative dentistry related clinical case scenarios and the linguistic variations introduced around the original dataset. Additionally, a descriptive qualitative analysis was performed on a subset of cases to evaluate the quality of reasoning generated by both models.
Methodology: One hundred single best answer MCQs were generated using standardised resources, constituting a benchmark dataset. Controlled linguistic variations were introduced around the original dataset; paraphrasing (sentence/clause rewording), perturbation (token-level substitutions), and permutation (answer-order shuffle). These case scenarios were presented to both models using a standardised prompt, and the performance metrics (accuracy/recall, F1 score) were computed. Agreement between and within models was analysed using Cohen's kappa, while paired differences were evaluated using McNemar's test with a significant p-value less than 0.05. Qualitative analysis was performed on a subset of the total sample, and the responses were evaluated on a 3-point Likert scale.
Results: GPT-5 Plus achieved 80% accuracy on benchmark dataset compared to 66% for Gemini 2.5 Flash (McNemar's p-value = 0.0066). When linguistic variations were introduced, the performance of GPT-5 Plus declined, with perturbation having the most significant effect (McNemar's p-value = 0.003). Gemini 2.5 Flash, on the other hand, though inferior initial performance on benchmark dataset, maintained uniform decision patterns across all transformations with no significant drop further. The descriptive qualitative analysis demonstrated an overall higher proportion of responses rated as good (8/10, 80% for original dataset; 7/10, 70% for linguistic variations) for Gemini 2.5 Flash as opposed to GPT-5 Plus.
Conclusion: GPT-5 Plus outperformed Gemini 2.5 Flash on benchmark dataset; however, it was sensitive to linguistic variations. Perturbation negatively influenced the performance of GPT-5 Plus, emphasising the need to further investigate the linguistic phenomenon that may have affected the model's degradation. Additionally, the descriptive qualitative analysis demonstrated relatively higher performance for Gemini 2.5 Flash compared to GPT-5 Plus on the original dataset and across linguistic variations. However, owing to the descriptive nature of findings and limited sample size, the results should be interpreted with caution.

title: Task-Shifting Mental Health at Scale: A Multilingual Conversational AI for Nigerian Youth in Yoruba, Hausa, Nigerian Pidgin, and English
abstract:
Background: Nigeria faces one of the world's largest mental health treatment gaps. With a population exceeding 200 million and a severe shortage of mental health specialists, many young people experiencing depression or anxiety do not receive appropriate care. Stigma and language barriers further limit help-seeking, while existing digital mental health tools rarely operate in the everyday languages used by Nigerian youth, reducing accessibility and trust.
Method: We developed BraveHeart AI, a multilingual conversational agent that provides first-line, low-stigma mental health support in Yoruba, Hausa, Nigerian Pidgin, and English. The system is delivered through WhatsApp, SMS, and the web so that young people can access support through familiar channels, including low-bandwidth connections and basic mobile phones. A unified language-detection and routing layer identifies users' preferred language and code-switching behaviour. Culturally grounded safety guardrails shape the chatbot's responses, while structured escalation pathways connect users showing indicators of elevated risk to human support and referral services rather than relying on the AI system to manage crises independently.
Results: During a three-month pilot, the platform supported 1,614 conversations from 796 unique users across four states. Most interactions were multilingual: 62.7% occurred in a language other than English, and automatic language detection achieved 96.3% accuracy. Among users who completed a brief mental health screening, 108 were directed to tailored self-help resources, while 16.8% received a recommendation to seek formal mental health services. Overall user satisfaction averaged 4.6 out of 5, and 10.9% of users disengaged before completing an initial support conversation.
Conclusion: The findings suggest that multilingual conversational AI can extend meaningful first-line mental health support to underserved young people while task-shifting routine screening and triage away from scarce mental health specialists. This allows limited clinical capacity to focus on higher-risk cases. The study also shows that accessibility in low-resource settings depends not only on model capability, but also on language, delivery channel, and trust. Support delivered in Yoruba, Hausa, Nigerian Pidgin, or English through familiar platforms such as WhatsApp can reach users who may not engage with English-only, app-based services. When paired with rigorous safety protocols and clear escalation pathways, this approach offers a scalable, culturally responsive complement to Nigeria's constrained mental health workforce and a practical model for multilingual youth mental health support across African settings.

title: Machine Learning-Based Forecasting of Monthly Pulmonology Admissions Using Climate Data in Douala, Cameroon
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory diseases place substantial pressure on health systems in sub-Saharan Africa, where hospital resources are constrained and service demand may vary according to temporal and environmental conditions. Reliable forecasting of hospital admissions could support proactive allocation of beds, healthcare personnel, oxygen, medicines, and other essential resources. However, evidence on the application of machine learning to forecast respiratory hospital demand remains limited in Central Africa. This study compared conventional time-series and machine-learning approaches for forecasting monthly admissions to the pulmonology unit of Douala General Hospital, Cameroon.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective time-series study using 180 monthly observations collected between January 2009 and December 2023. Monthly pulmonology admissions were linked with climate data obtained from the NASA POWER database, including ambient temperature, precipitation, and surface atmospheric pressure. Candidate predictors for the machine-learning models included admissions recorded during the previous one to three months, calendar month, and meteorological variables. Models were developed using data from January 2009 to December 2022 and evaluated on a chronological holdout set comprising the 12 months of 2023. Four forecasting approaches were compared: autoregressive integrated moving average, seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting. Predictive performance was assessed using root mean squared error, mean absolute error, mean absolute percentage error, and the coefficient of determination.
RESULT: Extreme Gradient Boosting achieved the best predictive performance, with an RMSE of 2.97 admissions, an MAE of 2.25 admissions, a MAPE of 16.83%, and an R-squared of 0.45. Random Forest achieved an RMSE of 3.54, an MAE of 2.84, and a MAPE of 22.87%, while ARIMA and SARIMA both produced an RMSE of 4.05, an MAE of 3.24, and a MAPE of 36.28%. Admissions recorded during the previous month were the most influential predictor in the Extreme Gradient Boosting model, followed by ambient temperature. These findings indicate that short-term admission history and environmental information contributed to forecasting monthly hospital demand.
CONCLUSION: Machine-learning models, particularly Extreme Gradient Boosting, showed better predictive accuracy than the conventional time-series approaches evaluated in this single-hospital study. Integrating routinely collected hospital data with climate information may support more proactive planning of pulmonology services in resource-constrained settings. Further temporal and external validation using data from additional hospitals is required before operational deployment.

title: From Reactive Mental Healthcare to Predictive Service Delivery: An AI-Enabled Behavioral Health Intelligence Framework for Strengthening Primary Health Systems in Africa
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health conditions account for a substantial proportion of the disease burden across low and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet health systems remain predominantly reactive, relying on patients to seek care only after significant psychological deterioration. In Africa, this challenge is compounded by severe workforce shortages, fragmented referral pathways, stigma, limited access to specialist services, and weak population-level behavioral health surveillance. While recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have accelerated interest in digital mental health, most implementations continue to function as standalone digital tools rather than integrated health system interventions. This paper proposes an AI-enabled behavioral health intelligence framework that strengthens primary healthcare through continuous risk identification, clinical decision support, and proactive service delivery.
METHODS: A health systems implementation framework was developed through the deployment of FriendnPal, a multilingual AI-enabled behavioral health platform operating across multiple African settings. The framework integrates validated behavioral health assessments, conversational large language models, natural language processing, digital phenotyping, longitudinal behavioral monitoring, automated risk stratification, and clinician-in-the-loop care pathways. Rather than replacing healthcare professionals, the system augments routine service delivery by supporting continuous screening, prioritization of high-risk individuals, remote monitoring, referral coordination, and population-level behavioral intelligence. Implementation was undertaken through partnerships involving healthcare providers, governments, universities, employers, humanitarian organizations, and community stakeholders.
RESULT: The implementation demonstrates the operational feasibility of embedding AI into routine behavioral healthcare delivery in resource-constrained environments. To date, the platform has supported more than 87,000 individuals, completed over 60,000 behavioral health assessments, and expanded access to culturally appropriate mental healthcare through multilingual digital channels. AI-assisted risk stratification enabled earlier identification of individuals requiring clinical intervention, while clinician-supported workflows improved prioritization of limited specialist resources. The accumulation of longitudinal behavioral health data further created opportunities for population-level surveillance, service planning, and evidence-informed policy development. The implementation illustrates how AI can strengthen continuity of care while extending health system capacity without proportionally increasing workforce demands.
CONCLUSION: Artificial intelligence should be viewed not simply as a clinical technology but as foundational infrastructure for modern health systems. AI-enabled behavioral health intelligence offers a scalable approach to strengthening primary healthcare by improving early detection, optimizing workforce allocation, enhancing continuity of care, and generating real-time evidence for health system planning. The FriendnPal implementation demonstrates that locally developed AI innovations can strengthen service delivery while supporting equitable, resilient, and data-driven health systems across Africa. As countries develop national AI strategies, integrating predictive behavioral intelligence into routine healthcare delivery represents an important pathway toward achieving universal health coverage and more proactive models of care.

title: Artificial Intelligence for suicide risk within mental health: A Scoping Synthesis of Data Sources, Methods, and Performance
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Applications of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning in mental health and suicide risk prevention have grown rapidly in recent years. However, existing research remains fragmented across data sources, methodological approaches, and clinical applications. Objective: This systematic review aims to synthesize empirical studies using AI, ML, and DL-based approaches for suicide related outcome within mental health, focus on data landscapes, methodological frameworks, and clinical evidence.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2015 and January 2026. A total of 9,423 records were identified from the databases. After removing duplicates, 5,890 records were screened, 148 full-text reports were assessed, resulting in 124 studies meeting the inclusion criteria.
RESULTS: Our finding revealed predictive modeling was the dominant approach, accounting for the majority of studies, with clinical data (31 studies) and social media data (32 studies) being the most common types of studies. ML methods, particularly tree-based ensemble models such as Random Forest and XGBoost, were widely used (around 78%), while DL approaches showed increasing adoption after 2020. Reported performance was high, with AUC values ranging from 0.62 to 0.98. However, only 14% of studies used 10-fold cross-validation, implementation research was limited, and handling of class imbalance was inconsistent (27% used SMOTE). Explainable AI methods appeared in 35% of studies, with SHAP being the most frequently used method.
CONCLUSION: Although AI-based models show promising results for suicide risk prediction and mental health assessment, significant challenges remain in translating these models into real-world clinical practice. Future research should consider external validation, clinician-centered implementation, and equitable model generalizability across diverse populations and healthcare settings.

title: Artifical intelligence mental health and suicide risk prediction
abstract: Now a day mental health and suicide risk become critical global public health challenges, with traditional risk detection methods limited by subjectivity, delayed diagnosis, and reliance on patient self-disclosure. Artificial intelligence and machine learning offer promising methods for analyzing behavioral and psychological patterns to enhance early risk identification. This study aims to evaluate the performance of four machine learning algorithms:- RF, DT, XGBoost, and SVM, in detecting mental health and suicide risk, while identifying the most influential behavioral and psychological features driving model predictions. A publicly available Kaggle dataset comprising 120 patient records with 18 behavioral attributes were trained and evaluated using two train-test split ratios (75:25 and 90:10) and 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices. The Random Forest model outperformed all other algorithms, achieving the highest accuracy of 90.00% (75:25 split), 100% (90:10 split), and 89.17% (5-fold cross-validation), while SVM showed the lowest performance across all evaluation conditions (73.33% to 74.17%). Feature importance and SHAP analysis shows that Mood swing, Optimism, and Sexual activity were the most influential predictors, whereas Suicidal thoughts showed only medium importance. The findings suggest that machine learning models may capture broader affective instability patterns rather than relying on explicit suicidal ideation reports. These results support the potential utility of AI-based decision support tools in resource limited clinical settings, though further validation with larger, more diverse datasets and ethical frameworks is required before real world deployment.

title: Exploring the Use of Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Virtual Reality in Teaching and Evaluating Communication Skills in Urology: A Pilot Study
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Effective communication is a core competency in healthcare, yet traditional training methods often face limitations in realism, scalability, and learner engagement. This study evaluated the perceptions of healthcare professionals regarding the use of artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced virtual reality (VR) simulations for communication skills training in urology.
METHODS: A total of 45 healthcare professionals (N = 45) participated in a haematuria role-play simulation using AI-enhanced VR via Bodyswaps software. Participants completed pre- and post-simulation questionnaires using a standard five-point Likert scale to measure perceptions of the potential of AI-VR to improve communication skills, usefulness, agreement with AI-generated feedback, realism compared to clinical practice, and overall enjoyability. Although Likert-scale responses are ordinal, they were treated as approximately interval data for statistical analysis. Descriptive statistics and one-sample t-tests against the neutral midpoint (3.0) were conducted to assess whether participant perceptions differed significantly from neutrality, with significance set at alpha = 0.05.
RESULTS: Prior to the simulation, participants (n = 23, 51.11%) reported belief in the potential of AI-VR to improve communication skills by responding above the neutral midpoint (M = 3.844, SD = 0.9034). Post-simulation, participants (n = 40, 88.89%) showed increased perceptions of usefulness (M = 4.636, SD = 0.6851). High levels of agreement with AI-generated feedback were reported by participants (n = 35, 77.78%) (M = 4.2, SD = 0.9195), and participants (n = 40, 88.89%) rated the simulation as useful (M = 4.5, SD = 0.6949). Regarding realism, participants (n = 34, 73.33%) rated the simulation positively (M = 4.159, SD = 0.9135), and participants (n = 41, 91.11%) found the experience enjoyable (M = 4.465, SD = 0.8549). All results reached statistical significance (p less than 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that AI-enhanced VR simulations have potential as effective and engaging tools for communication skills training in urology. The positive responses across all measured domains support further integration of immersive AI technologies into clinical education.

title: Clinician-Supervised AI Monitoring Platform for Early Deterioration Detection and Safer Post-Discharge Care
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospitals in resource-constrained settings often depend on fragmented and reactive monitoring systems. Clinical deterioration may be detected late because vital signs, electronic health records, bedside observations, patient-reported symptoms, and post-discharge communication are poorly integrated. These gaps contribute to delayed intervention, avoidable adverse events, unnecessary readmissions, overcrowding, staff burden, and poorer patient experience. Low-income and vulnerable patients are particularly affected because delayed detection can increase out-of-pocket costs, repeated hospital visits, lost income, and preventable complications. This abstract presents a clinician-supervised AI monitoring and diagnostic model designed to support early deterioration detection, safer post-discharge care, and improved hospital workflow.
METHODS: The proposed innovation integrates five components: a clinician dashboard, patient mobile app, cloud-based AI analytics core, HL7 FHIR-enabled interoperability layer, and embedded AI governance layer. The clinician dashboard displays risk scores, predictive alerts, diagnostic insights, and patient follow-up indicators. The patient app supports symptom reporting, reminders, secure communication, teleconsultation, and optional wearable integration. The AI analytics core combines hospital and patient-generated data to identify clinical deterioration risk earlier than routine episodic monitoring. The governance layer includes explainability, audit trails, clinician sign-off, bias monitoring, transparency review, and safety oversight. The proposed pilot follows a Hybrid Type 2 implementation-effectiveness design, assessing feasibility, workflow fit, predictive performance, patient engagement, safety, governance compliance, and early cost-effectiveness.
EXPECTED RESULTS: The pilot is expected to generate early evidence on whether the platform can improve time to deterioration detection, clinician response to high-risk alerts, post-discharge continuity, patient engagement, and governance readiness. Model performance will be assessed using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, calibration, false-alert review, and subgroup fairness checks. Implementation outcomes will include clinician usability, patient app use, alert acknowledgement, response time, workflow acceptability, and cost per patient monitored.
CONCLUSION: This innovation offers a scalable, clinician-supervised approach to AI-enabled service delivery in hospitals. By combining predictive analytics, patient engagement, interoperability, secure communication, and accountable AI governance, the model can support safer, earlier, and more coordinated care. The proposed pilot will generate practical evidence for future deployment across hospitals in Nigeria and other resource-constrained health systems.

title: An AI-Driven Framework for Identifying Cognitive Resilience Despite Progressive Brain Atrophy in Older Adults
abstract:
Background: As populations age globally, preserving cognitive health has become a major public health priority. While most artificial intelligence (AI) applications in aging research focus on predicting cognitive decline and dementia, substantially less attention has been devoted to identifying individuals who maintain cognitive function despite progressive brain deterioration. Understanding such resilience mechanisms may inform future strategies for healthy aging, early intervention, and population-level brain health planning. This study developed and evaluated an AI-driven framework for discovering and characterizing cognitive resilience using longitudinal aging data.
Methods: Data were obtained from the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS-2), comprising 373 longitudinal observations from 150 older adults aged 60-96 years. A multi-stage analytical pipeline integrated unsupervised machine learning, longitudinal trajectory modeling, predictive analytics, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). K-means clustering was used to identify latent resilience phenotypes based on demographic, cognitive, and MRI-derived neuroanatomical measures. Longitudinal cognitive and atrophy trajectories were subsequently modeled at the participant level. A Longitudinal Cognitive Resilience Index (LCRI) and a machine-learning-derived Resilience Gap framework were developed to quantify cognitive performance relative to expected decline. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were applied to identify factors contributing to resilience.
Results: Three distinct aging phenotypes emerged from clustering analyses, including a cognitively resilient subgroup that maintained higher cognitive performance despite levels of brain atrophy comparable to vulnerable individuals. Longitudinal analyses identified 15 resilient and 15 vulnerable participants among 150 individuals. Notably, model-based resilient and vulnerable groups exhibited nearly identical baseline atrophy burdens (0.273 vs. 0.279) but markedly different final cognitive outcomes (MMSE: 27.33 vs. 20.13). Gradient Boosting achieved the highest classification performance (AUROC = 0.815) for identifying resilient individuals. Explainable AI analyses demonstrated that baseline cognitive performance, brain atrophy, intracranial volume, education, and socioeconomic status were among the most influential contributors to resilience.
Conclusions: This study demonstrates the potential of AI to identify hidden resilience phenotypes and characterize heterogeneous aging trajectories beyond conventional disease-focused approaches. The findings suggest that individuals with comparable neuroanatomical burden may experience substantially different cognitive outcomes and highlight the value of AI-driven approaches for population-level brain health surveillance, healthy aging initiatives, and future precision public health strategies.

title: Caught Before the Fall: Decoding the Digital Prodrome of Vasovagal Syncope through Wearable Autonomic Intelligence
abstract:
Background: Every year, patients with vasovagal syncope (VVS) collapse without warning, on staircases, behind steering wheels, alone at home. Responsible for 30-40% of all syncope, VVS is common yet catastrophically unpredictable. The mechanism is an autonomic ambush: sympathetic overstimulation followed by vagal overdrive drains cerebral perfusion in seconds. Most feel nothing until they fall. This review asks: can a smartwatch see what the patient cannot feel?
Methods: Not only did we search the literature; but also examined it rigorously. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were systematically searched (years 2020-2026), with exclusion criteria being case studies, prototypes without validation, and non-peer-reviewed abstracts. Data was examined from five perspectives: sensors, prodrome biomarkers, autonomic phenotype, prediction modeling, and clinical translation paradigms.
Results: The findings redefine what consumer technology is capable of clinically. A Samsung Galaxy Watch predicted VVS across 132 patients with an AUROC of 0.91, rivalling hospital-grade cardiac monitors. Remarkably, wearable-derived heart rate variability can accurately predict tilt-induced syncope (AUROC approximately 0.91) starting five minutes before pre-syncope begins. Specifically, during pre-syncope, parameters like the standard deviation of NN interval (SDNN), root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), and the percentage of adjacent RR intervals differing by more than 50 ms (pNN50), along with approximate entropy and multiscale entropy, can discriminate this period. Pre-syncope is also characterized by a rise in electrodermal activity (EDA) that can precede a blood pressure fall by approximately 257 seconds, doing so in approximately two-thirds of patients. Among the models, ensemble trees and gradient-boosted machines perform best in this prediction in children and adults alike. In pediatric cohorts, nonlinear HRV indices with anthropometric variables achieved 71% predictive accuracy without blood pressure input.
Conclusion: This is not a study about fainting, it is a blueprint for predictive medicine. The pre-syncopal stage gives off clear physiological signals on wearables; combining PPG and EDA with machine learning lets us build a practical, online prediction system. Multi-center ambulatory validation, federated learning, and regulatory recognition of wearable warnings as clinical tools are the field's urgent next steps. The technology is no longer the barrier. The next collapse that does not happen, because a wristwatch warned in time, is the milestone this work is building toward.

title: Ayooka: An AI-Driven National Blood Transfusion Information System to Strengthen Transfusion Safety and Efficiency in Guinea
abstract:
Background: Blood transfusion is essential to emergency care, surgery, obstetric complications, and the management of many chronic conditions. In Guinea, national blood needs are estimated at approximately 525,635 units for 2026, while current collection covers less than half of this demand. This structural deficit is compounded by limited digitalization of transfusion processes, poor visibility over available stocks, weak coordination between actors, partial traceability of blood products, and avoidable losses through expiry. Together, these gaps degrade quality of care and undermine the system's capacity to respond to patient needs.
Methods: Ayooka is a national digital information and management system covering the full transfusion cycle from donor to recipient within an integrated, modular, and interoperable platform. Beyond digitalizing core processes (donor management, collection campaigns, laboratory and qualification, real-time multi-bank stock management, transfusion requests, hemovigilance, and end-to-end traceability), the system embeds an artificial intelligence layer that anticipates shortages, forecasts needs by period, region, and product type, optimizes stock levels, and reduces expiry-related losses. The architecture is designed for low-connectivity environments (offline mode) and enforces in-country data residency, end-to-end encryption, role-based access control, and a complete audit trail, ensuring data sovereignty and compliance. The pilot was deployed under real-world conditions in Conakry, with impact measured against pre-digitalization, paper-register baselines.
Results: The pilot phase demonstrated measurable operational impact: a 78% reduction in unit losses, a 64% reduction in the time required to locate blood, a 40% increase in inter-bank transfers, and a 38% increase in satisfaction in emergency settings. At one pilot site, the blood product loss rate fell from 8.1% to 1.4% over a single year, reflecting the shift from paper-based management to networked, real-time coordination. These results validate the operational relevance of the solution and its potential for national-scale impact.
Conclusions: Ayooka demonstrates how sovereign digital infrastructure, coupled with predictive AI and strong institutional anchoring, can transform a critical yet often neglected component of African health systems. The project is governed through a dual institutional mandate: the Ministry of Health and Public Hygiene (National Blood Transfusion Center) and the Ministry of Digital Affairs (ANSUTEN), illustrating a genuinely country-led model of AI in health. With a phased national rollout underway and regional ECOWAS extension planned, Ayooka offers a reproducible blueprint for country-led AI adoption that strengthens transfusion safety and equitable access to blood across Africa and beyond.

title: ABIYAMO: Governance Lessons from a Responsible AI Framework for Sexual and Reproductive Health Communication Among Nigerian Adolescents
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sexual and reproductive health (SRH) remains deeply stigmatised among Nigerian adolescents aged 16 to 24, with social barriers and fear of judgment limiting access to professional care. As young people increasingly turn to general-purpose large language models (LLMs) for health guidance, their use in sensitive healthcare contexts raises governance concerns around safety, accountability, data protection, and equitable access. These challenges are particularly relevant in low-resource settings where inappropriate AI deployment may increase risks of misinformation and delayed care.
METHOD: Abiyamo was developed as a responsible AI chatbot for SRH education among Nigerian youth and evaluated as a case study of how responsible AI requirements can be operationalised in healthcare. The system uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation grounded in validated Federal Ministry of Health and WHO SRH resources and supports English, Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo. A two-layer intent detection mechanism combining deterministic keyword matching and fine-tuned DistilBERT distinguishes educational, diagnostic, and crisis queries. Diagnostic and crisis queries bypass AI generation and are routed to verified Nigerian health facility referrals and the national emergency number. Interaction data is anonymised using SHA-256 hashing before logging, with data handling aligned with the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA) 2023.
RESULT: The fine-tuned DistilBERT model achieved a crisis recall of 0.909 at an adjusted classification threshold, exceeding the a priori safety target of 0.80 and outperforming the TF-IDF baseline, which achieved 0.818. Educational query classification achieved an F1 score of 0.882. Crisis recall was prioritised because failure to identify a user in crisis carries greater potential harm than a false positive referral.
CONCLUSION: Abiyamo demonstrates how responsible AI principles can be translated into practical safeguards and measurable controls for healthcare deployment. The implementation provides governance lessons for Nigeria, particularly the need for defined AI-use boundaries, risk-sensitive evaluation, locally validated knowledge, linguistic inclusion, data protection, and human escalation mechanisms to support national AI health standards and responsible AI adoption.

title: Developing Smart Policies: An AI Framework for Integrating Multisectoral Insights into Nigerian Government Health Systems
abstract:
Background: AI-driven health surveillance and natural language processing (NLP) tools have improved data synthesis and decision support in global health systems.
